clue.text: Experts eat cheese with holes in regularly

indicators.note: a cheese full of holes at even intervals keeps only every other letter of the words eat cheese

explanation.surface: A claim that the real connoisseurs eat Swiss-style cheese full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with holes in regularly' drops the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of EATCHEESE, leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is someone highly skilled at something, a synonym for an expert.

clue.text: Happy to have home within Europe, perhaps

indicators.note: home goes within the word for happy

parts.note: content means happy or satisfied
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone happy to make a home somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one of the world's great landmasses, an example of such a landmass.

clue.text: Do guzzle cold dessert? No time!

indicators.note: time is T, and there is none of it, so the T goes

parts.note: to stuff oneself is to guzzle
an ice is an ice cream, a cold dessert

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they should gobble an ice cream when time is short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the verb meaning 'be enough', as in 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enough or adequate, as in that will do, is to be sufficient.

clue.text: Newspaper reviewers write so seriously?

definitions.meaning: critics in a newspaper write in the manner of critics, finding fault and judging
gravely, as in being badly ill or injured

explanation.surface: Wondering whether newspaper reviewers write with real gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is playful: critics naturally write in a critic's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dangerously ill is being ill in a grave way, so the adverb pairs with serious harm.

clue.text: Seasonal song Lorca composed

indicators.note: composed suggests putting together, so the letters of the poet's name are arranged anew

explanation.surface: The poet Lorca writes a Christmas song.
explanation.walkthrough: Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas hymn sung at the festive season, a seasonal song.

clue.text: In sea-going vessel, loud noise interrupting speech shows disrespect for authority

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel at sea

indicators.note: the noise breaks into the speech, sitting inside it

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Aboard ship, heckling during a captain's address shows disrespect.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusal to obey superiors, especially in the military, is defiance of authority.

clue.text: Member of ancient civilisation destroyed, you might say? Wrong

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: an Inca was a member of the ancient Peruvian civilisation; destroyed is wrecked

explanation.surface: Questions whether calling an Inca destroyed is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inca wrecked' spoken quickly matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong is mistaken or not accurate.

clue.text: American with a joie de vivre that's awesome

parts.note: zing is zest or liveliness, joy in living

explanation.surface: An American with zest for life is admired as awesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome and wonderful both mean causing great wonder or astonishment.

clue.text: Primate is following God no end

indicators.note: the word is comes after the shortened God
the last letter of the word for God is cut off

parts.note: the Lord is God

explanation.surface: A primate that follows God endlessly, as if a worshipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop, given 'God', but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-moving nocturnal Asian animal, one of the primate group with lemurs.

clue.text: Clothes worn in school and higher education classes

parts.note: uni is short for university, the place of higher education
forms are school classes or year groups in British schools

explanation.surface: A list of what students wear in school and at university and in lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a British school class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at many schools must wear a set outfit, the standard dress of the school.

clue.text: Girl's secluded spot in church

indicators.note: the secluded spot sits inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lair is a hidden den or retreat

explanation.surface: A girl has her own quiet hiding place inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so a girl can be one of that name.

clue.text: In places like London, reflected about William IV's personal rights

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go into the places, which hold them

parts.note: London is an example of a city, so places like it are cities

indicators.note: reflected in a mirror, so the pieces read from back to front

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Bill is a short form of William

explanation.surface: A historical note on what King William IV did about personal freedoms in cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is a decoy: William and the numeral split apart, and 'reflected' turns all three pieces backwards as VILLIBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedoms of speech, assembly and so on are the rights belonging to each individual citizen.

clue.text: Commemorate someone who joined the Royal Engineers?

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
one who has joined a body is a member of it

explanation.surface: Asks whether one should honour a soldier who enlisted in the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To commemorate the dead is to recall and honour them, a synonym for that kind of recall.

clue.text: A weapon concealed in cracker? It's of little importance

indicators.note: the pieces are hidden away inside the cracker

parts.note: a cracker is slang for a beautiful woman, a belle
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A toy weapon hidden in a Christmas cracker is trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracker' looks like a Christmas cracker but means an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle, something trivial or unimportant, from French for a trinket.

clue.text: Hunters taking lead off dogs

indicators.note: the lead is the front letter, which comes off the dogs

parts.note: beagles are a breed of hunting dog

explanation.surface: Someone unclips the leads from a pack of hunting dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog lead but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of prey such as these hunt small animals, so they are predators.

clue.text: Large cars equipped with one metre gauges

indicators.note: the cars hold the other letters inside them

parts.note: estates are estate cars, roomy vehicles
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Big cars fitted with a single measuring instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gauges' is a verb here, not a noun for dials.
explanation.definitionFit: To gauge something is to judge or reckon it roughly.

clue.text: Way convict goes around a prison camp

indicators.note: the street and convict pair wrap around the letter a

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a lag is an old lag, slang for a convict

explanation.surface: Describes a prisoner walking a path around a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A wartime German camp for captured soldiers, specifically a prisoner-of-war camp.

clue.text: Middle part of evening during pre-Easter period is mild

indicators.note: the middle letters come within the pre-Easter period

parts.note: Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: the central three letters are taken from the word

explanation.surface: An evening in Lent proves gentle and mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle part of' takes ENI from EVENING.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciful and not harsh, as a judge giving a gentle sentence.

clue.text: Suggest I should avoid bully

indicators.note: the letters for I should keep away from the bully, so they are dropped

parts.note: to intimidate is to bully or frighten
I'd is the contraction of I should or I would

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I should' is not advice here: it is the contraction I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without saying it outright is to suggest it.

clue.text: One having hair specially styled in macho fashion?

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A person with a striking hairstyle in a tough-guy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a person who wears the famous crested haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sporting the Mohican style, a strip of hair down the centre of the shaved head.

clue.text: In the words of the song, it's anathema travelling round Panama, perhaps

definitions.text: In the words of the song

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the hat
letters on the move are rearranged

parts.note: a Panama is a type of straw hat

explanation.surface: A traveller loathes going around Panama, said in song lyric style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges ITSANATHEMA to AINTTASHAME, which goes round HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Domino's hit song title, so the words come from that famous rock and roll record.

clue.text: Site of battle in Kampala mountain

indicators.note: the answer lies within the words Kampala mountain

explanation.surface: A battlefield in a mountain near the Ugandan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texan mission where the 1836 siege took place is a famous battlefield.

clue.text: Helpful person I read about

indicators.note: about means around and here signals the letters being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: I read up on someone helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives help or assistance is a helper.

clue.text: Nurse keeping a volume in cubicle

indicators.note: the cubicle keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: a cell is a small room or cubicle

explanation.surface: A nurse keeps a book in a small hospital cubicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Cavell was a British First World War nurse executed for helping soldiers escape.

clue.text: Guy is engaged by record company for show

indicators.note: the fellow is taken on within the company's letters

parts.note: an indie is an independent record label
cat is jazz slang for a man, a guy

explanation.surface: A man is signed up by a record label to perform in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a verb here, as in point out.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out or demonstrate something is to show it.

clue.text: Middlesex inhabitant possibly bitter about the old railway company

indicators.note: the sour letters go around the word the

parts.note: sour means bitter or acid
NER was the North Eastern Railway, a pre-1923 British railway company

explanation.surface: A Middlesex resident grumbles bitterly about an old railway firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Middlesex is a former county in the south of England, round London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Middlesex lives in the south of England, so is an example of one from the south.

clue.text: Boy brought round hot food

indicators.note: turned round, so the boy's letters read backwards

parts.note: a son is a boy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A lad comes over bringing hot food.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for food or a meal.
